claim: In process, on the repository's offline upload world with seven synthetic sheets (28 writer/reader cases), every template that was stored was re-opened by read_input and re-POSTed under the reader that ran the re-open: 16 of 16 ACCEPTED (8 same-version, 8 mixed). The 8 mixed re-opens ran no full re-read comparison (compare_runs_on_reopen false in 8 of 8), which is the only reason none of them refused; the 8 same-version re-opens ran it and passed. So in this set no input accepted under one version was refused by the other at re-open. The versions differ at the upload DOOR, not at re-open: the same bytes can be stored by one version and turned back by the other. Two valid one-account files were checked: the repaired reader accepts both, and the round-16 reader turns back the one with an 'Account Value' column (a false refusal). The two inputs the repaired reader turns back (a total row, a two-value Account column) are turned back by the round-16 reader too, except the hyphenated 'Account-Number' two-value sheet, which the round-16 reader stores. NOT shown: the deployed Lambda's own bytes, the resident's installed package, the resolve path with request_resolution wired, and the queue between the two runtimes.

what_a_person_sees: Upload door, mixed state. The answer depends on which reader answers the POST, not on the file alone. A total-row sheet and a two-value 'Account' column are turned back by both versions. A two-value 'Account-Number' sheet is turned back by the repaired reader only: the round-16 reader stores it as NORMALIZED, so a person uploading it through an old runtime sees a success for a file with two accounts. A one-account file with an 'Account Value' column is turned back by the round-16 reader (ACCOUNT_COLUMN_SEVERAL_VALUES on a column that is not an account number) and accepted by the repaired reader. Same-token re-POST: when the first answer was NORMALIZED, the re-POST returns the stored NORMALIZED under either reader, because the normalization row is not judged again; when the first answer was a turn-back, the re-POST is judged afresh by the reader that answers it. So one two-account file can read NORMALIZED on a same-token re-POST and NEEDS_CORRECTION on a fresh-token POST under the repaired reader (measured: writer round-16, repaired reader, repair_header_two_values). Re-open (portfolio, submit, refresh): a person sees no refusal caused by a version change; an input stored under either version opens under the other, and it is shown as the version that stored it decided it. The SHEETS_NOT_READ notice is stored by both versions on a two-sheet workbook. Not measured here: the words a portal shows for each code (only the state, reason and codes were recorded).
